{{Short description|None}}
{{Use mdy dates|date=December 2019}}
This is a '''list of [[New Jersey Devils]] head coaches'''. The Devils had 20 different head coaches since the team moved to New Jersey in the [[1982–83 NHL season|1982–83]], with [[Jacques Lemaire]] serving as coach three times and [[Tom McVie]], [[Larry Robinson]], and [[Lou Lamoriello]] each serving twice.

Three coaches have led the team to a victory in the [[Stanley Cup Final]]: Lemaire in [[1994–95 NHL season|1995]], Robinson in [[1999–2000 NHL season|2000]], and [[Pat Burns]] in [[2003 Stanley Cup Playoffs|2003]]. Lemaire is the all-time leader in games coached and wins, while Burns leads in winning percentage (with at least one full season coached).

Several former players have worked for the Devils as assistant coaches, including [[John MacLean (ice hockey)|John MacLean]] and [[Bobby Carpenter (ice hockey)|Bobby Carpenter]], the only men whose names are inscribed on the Stanley Cup as both a player and a coach with New Jersey. MacLean later served as head coach and is the only former Devils' player to serve in that capacity.

On December 26, 2014, after the firing of DeBoer, head coaching responsibilities were split between [[Adam Oates]] and [[Scott Stevens]] for the remainder of the 2014–15 season, with Lamoriello supervising the team from the bench.<ref>{{cite web |title=Devils name Stevens, Oates to replace DeBoer |url=https://www.nhl.com/devils/news/devils-name-stevens-oates-to-replace-deboer/c-745751 |website=NHL.com |access-date=December 12, 2019 |date=December 27, 2014 |archive-date=December 12, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191212200648/https://www.nhl.com/devils/news/devils-name-stevens-oates-to-replace-deboer/c-745751 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Vorkunov |first1=Mike |title=Devils will have 'unique' head-coaching situation: Co-coaches Adam Oates and Scott Stevens |url=https://www.nj.com/devils/2014/12/devils_name_new_coach.html |website=NJ.com |access-date=December 13, 2019 |date=December 27, 2014 |archive-date=December 13, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191213125623/https://www.nj.com/devils/2014/12/devils_name_new_coach.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Notes==
<!-- This section is for footnotes and footnotes only, no references. Place the ref template behind the persons name. To use footnotes, use the templates here: http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Footnote3#How to use-->
#{{note|Win–loss percentage}} The win–loss percentage is calculated using the formula: <math>\frac{Wins+\frac{1}{2}Ties}{Games}</math>
#{{note|Devilsmovedate}} Since the Devils officially finalized their move [[Colorado Rockies (NHL)|from Colorado]] to New Jersey on June 30, 1982, that is the date that their reign as coach and assistant coach began on the Devils.
#{{note|Schoenfeldsuspended}} Schoenfeld was suspended for one game during the [[1988 Stanley Cup playoffs]] for verbally abusing referee [[Don Koharski]]; [[General Manager (ice hockey)|general manager]] [[Lou Lamoriello]] filled in as coach for the Devils' 7–1 loss to [[Boston Bruins|Boston]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nysun.com/article/51728?page_no=3|title=Lamoriello Fires Julien, Takes Over Behind Devils' Bench|publisher=[[New York Sun]]|author=Kevin Greenstein|date=April 3, 2007|access-date=June 16, 2007|archive-date=September 29, 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070929130622/http://www.nysun.com/article/51728?page_no=3|url-status=live}}</ref>
#{{note|Ftorekcupafterwards}} Although Ftorek was replaced during the [[1999–2000 NHL season|1999–2000 season]], he got his name on the Cup when the Devils won it later that same season.
#{{note|Robinsoncupafterwards}} Robinson was demoted to assistant coach and replaced as head coach in the middle of the [[2001–02 NHL season|2001–02 season]], but the Devils placed his name on the Cup when they won the following season even though he had left before the [[2002–03 NHL season|2002–03 season]] even began.
#{{note|PatBurnscancer}} Pat Burns resigned after being diagnosed with cancer.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/hockey/larry-robinson-named-devils-coach-1.559451|title=Larry Robinson named Devils' coach|publisher=[[CBC Sports]]|access-date=December 13, 2019|date=July 14, 2005|archive-date=August 20, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210820085431/https://www.cbc.ca/sports/hockey/larry-robinson-named-devils-coach-1.559451|url-status=live}}</ref>
#{{note|LarryRobinsonstress}} Larry Robinson resigned due to stress-related health problems.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/hockey/larry-robinson-resigns-as-devils-coach-1.526733|title=Larry Robinson resigns as Devils coach|publisher=[[CBC Sports]]|access-date=December 13, 2019|date=December 21, 2005|archive-date=May 16, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210516211101/https://www.cbc.ca/sports/hockey/larry-robinson-resigns-as-devils-coach-1.526733|url-status=live}}</ref>
#{{note|ClaudeJulien3gamesleft}} Claude Julien was fired with just 3 games left in the [[2006–07 NHL season|2006–07 regular season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nhl/news/story?id=2822234|title=Julien out, Lamoriello in as Devils prepare for playoffs|date=April 2, 2007 |publisher=[[ESPN]]|access-date=June 17, 2007|archive-date=May 16, 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070516071444/http://sports.espn.go.com/nhl/news/story?id=2822234|url-status=live}}</ref>
#{{note|BrentSutterFamily}} Brent Sutter quit after two years of a three-year contract, citing a desire to be closer to home in Alberta, with his family and minor league hockey team, the [[Red Deer Rebels]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.upi.com/Sports_News/2009/06/09/Sutter-quits-as-NJ-Devils-coach/UPI-11021244566294/|title=Sutter quits as N.J. Devils' coach|publisher=UPI|date=June 9, 2009|access-date=July 10, 2009|archive-date=June 5, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110605065429/http://www.upi.com/Sports_News/2009/06/09/Sutter-quits-as-NJ-Devils-coach/UPI-11021244566294/|url-status=live}}</ref>  Several weeks later, Sutter was announced as the head coach of the [[Calgary Flames]].  Despite the fact that Calgary had to request permission to talk to Sutter, the Devils received no compensation.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://njmg.typepad.com/devilsblog/2009/06/brent-sutter-named-head-coach-of-the-calgary-flames.html|title=Brent Sutter named head coach of the Calgary Flames|publisher=[[Bergen Record]]|author=Tom Gulitti|date=June 23, 2009|access-date=July 10, 2009|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090627042059/http://njmg.typepad.com/devilsblog/2009/06/brent-sutter-named-head-coach-of-the-calgary-flames.html|archive-date=June 27, 2009}}</ref>
